standard.title: Experiences of individuals in establishing the first British colony
standard.description: the experiences of individuals and groups, including military and civilian officials, and convicts involved in the establishment of the first British colony
standard.prior_knowledge: From AC9HS4K02: Students explained causes of the first British colony. They now examine who was involved and what they experienced.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe the experiences of diverse individuals and groups involved in establishing the first British colony.

nodes.label: Who was on the First Fleet
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the different groups of people on the First Fleet and describe the range of backgrounds and reasons for their presence.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three different groups on the First Fleet (e.g. convicts, marines, officials, chaplain) and describe each group's role.
nodes.typical_width: Describe events around the establishment of the First Fleet and key people (Captain Phillip, marines, Reverend Johnson, convicts); examine the range of crimes punishable by transportation; investigate social standing of all groups who travelled.
wider: Research the experiences of a specific individual on the First Fleet (convict, marine or official) in depth
Investigate the particular experiences of children, families and women on the First Fleet
nodes.hinge_reason: Knowing who was on the First Fleet is prerequisite to describing their experiences — without this population knowledge, individual account analysis lacks context.

response_modes.reason: Students need to know who the groups were and why they were there before they can engage with individual experiences.

success_criteria: Names at least three different groups on the First Fleet
Describes the role or reason for each group's presence

nodes.label: Experiences during the journey and early settlement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the experiences of specific groups and individuals on the journey of the First Fleet and in the early Port Jackson settlement.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two challenges experienced by people on the First Fleet journey or in early settlement.
nodes.typical_width: Describe events and experiences of groups and individuals on the First Fleet journey; investigate daily life in the Port Jackson penal settlement; examine challenges experienced and how they were managed; investigate attitudes to the poor and social standing.
wider: Compare experiences of convicts with those of marines or officials during the same period
Investigate how the extreme conditions of early settlement affected different groups differently

response_modes.reason: Comparison across groups (convicts vs marines vs officials) reveals that the 'same' historical event was experienced very differently depending on social position.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing experiences across social groups teaches the historical thinking skill that the same event can have radically different meanings depending on who you are.
success_criteria: Describes at least two challenges experienced by people in early settlement
Identifies at least one difference in experience between two different groups
